variants.name: Channel observer list (hand-written)
variants.idiom_name: std::function observer list on the channel plus a copy queue
variants.implementation_notes: The classic structure is hand-written: the channel keeps a list of std::function<void(const Message&)> tap callbacks (or a second queue) and every publish forwards the message to the primary consumer and hands an independent copy to each tap. std::function is the polymorphic callback wrapper, so taps are registered without a class hierarchy; the copy must be explicit (serialize or deep-copy the payload), because handing the observer the live object lets the analyzer mutate or destroy what the primary path still uses. Choose this form when no messaging library is in the stack or when the tap attaches to an in-house channel abstraction - the classic form is what the library would otherwise hide from you.
pitfalls: Passing the live message to the observer is an aliasing and lifetime bug: copy first and document who owns the copy.
Invoking taps inside publish() makes tap latency part of the flow - hand the copy to a queue and dispatch it on a worker thread instead.
Taps registered without an unregister path keep captured objects alive and leak when components are destroyed.

variants.name: ZeroMQ proxy with a capture socket
variants.implementation_notes: ZeroMQ ships the tap inside its proxy: when the capture argument is not NULL, zmq_proxy sends all messages received on both the frontend and the backend to the capture socket, which must be a ZMQ_PUB, ZMQ_DEALER, ZMQ_PUSH or ZMQ_PAIR socket. On an XSUB/XPUB forwarder this captures every proxied message without touching either application, but the capture is best-effort: on a PUB capture socket a slow analyzer simply loses messages. Use when ZeroMQ is already the transport and the copy may be sampled or lossy; the capture also sees subscription traffic, so the analyzer must filter.
pitfalls: Capture is best-effort: with a slow tap consumer a PUB-style capture drops messages, so the copy must not be treated as a durable record.
An XSUB/XPUB capture sees subscription messages as well as payload, so the analyzer has to filter what it inspects.

zmq_proxy forwards to the capture socket only if it is a ZMQ_PUB, ZMQ_DEALER, ZMQ_PUSH or ZMQ_PAIR socket: binding the capture as, say, ZMQ_PULL or ZMQ_SUB is a misuse the proxy does not diagnose, so the tap silently carries no traffic.
